aiyalaeho-bilingual.note: 'a'iyalaeho: 開會了 - one Formosan row above one Chinese row, on an opaque yellow-to-red gradient band at the foot of the frame. The band is a saturated colour, so the plain white-pixel test is enough and the dark-outline one is not needed; `band_probe` reads a slice of the left edge the text never reaches, which is what tells a frame with no band (titles, credits) from one carrying a subtitle. Measured over 12 samples in each of the 38 subtitled episodes, the band drifts by episode: the Formosan row runs y=893..947 and the Chinese row y=950..1011, so the Chinese slot runs to y=1012 rather than stopping at 1008: three episodes (094, 111, 117) put its glyph bottoms at 1008..1011 and a 60px slot clipped them. Not to the region's foot at 1014, though -- the strip height feeds the contact sheet's packing budget, and at 66px a cue's block came to 560px against a 558px budget, which dropped the sheets from four cues to three and would have cost a third more reading for two pixels. Measured below 1011 there is nothing to keep: ink per row is 2 and 1 at y=1012 and 1013 on 094, and zero on 068. The top row is named `formosan`, not for any one language: this programme covers eleven of them and the row carries whichever the episode is in, Chinese words included where the speaker used them. SELECT THIS WITH `--preset`: file names in this corpus carry no reliable common substring, so there is deliberately no `match` here.
